data.description:
## Description
**What**: Implement a PreToolUse hook that reads the active (skill, phase) from durable session state, looks up the forbidden set in the registry (draft-1), and blocks an in-flight tool call when its tool/action class is forbidden for that phase, emitting a structured error directing the agent to complete the prerequisite phase work or surface to the user for an override.
**Why**: This is the enforcement spine of the epic — it converts documented HARD-GATEs into tool-use-time blocks. It also carries the false-positive invariant: happy-path tool calls must pass through unblocked.
**Scope**:
- IN: Reading active phase from durable session state, registry lookup, block decision, structured block error message, pass-through for non-forbidden calls, the fixture where an Edit during brainstorm Phase 1 is blocked, and a happy-path trace test covering brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan flows that asserts no spurious blocks.
- OUT: Registry enumeration (draft-1); the override CLI and audit trail (draft-3).

## Done Definitions

- An agent attempting Edit during brainstorm Phase 1 is blocked by the hook, with a structured error naming the active (skill, phase) and the forbidden tool ← Satisfies: sc-1
- A tool call whose tool/action class is not forbidden for the active phase passes through the hook without a block ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, the hook derives the active (skill, phase) by reading the same durable session-state artifact the brainstorm/sprint/fix-bug/implementation-plan skills already write for resume rather than a hook-private phase store, verified by a test that drives the hook from a skill-written phase artifact ← Satisfies: sc-1
- A happy-path end-to-end trace for each of brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan runs with the hook active and produces no spurious blocks ← Validates Closure Check: "Zero false positives on representative session-level traces of brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan flows (each runs a happy-path session end-to-end with the new hook active and produces no spurious blocks)."
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including the phase-state read, the block decision, and the pass-through path ← Satisfies: sc-1

## Considerations

- [Reliability] The false-positive trace test is the cc-1 guard; a single spurious block on any of the four happy-path flows fails the story.
- [Convention] The hook .sh file sets the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation; non-executable hooks are silently skipped by the gate.
- [Consistency] The hook reads the skills' own durable resume artifact for active (skill, phase); a hook-private phase store would drift from the skills' resume state and produce spurious or missed blocks.
- [External-blocker] Session-state-aware hook installation reuses the sibling-epic (d076-d35e, 750c-6033) pattern; no in-epic depends_on is created for that outside infra.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a sub-agent operator, I want a phase-aware PreToolUse hook that blocks tool calls forbidden by the active phase, so HARD-GATEs are load-bearing during silent execution rather than only when challenged
